# Randomly Partition Array

## Problem

An integer array `nums` of length `n` and an integer `k` are given. Randomly divide `nums` into `k` groups such that every group contains exactly `n / k` values.

Every value in `nums` must be placed into exactly one group, and no value may be repeated across groups. The result should be `k` lists of identical size, representing one possible random partition.

Because the partition is random, more than one output may be valid for the same input. You may assume that `n` is always divisible by `k`.

**Constraints:**

- $$1 \le k \le n \le 1000$$
- All elements of `nums` are integers in the range `[-1000, 1000]`.

**Example 1:**

> **Input:** nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], k = 2
> **Output:** [[2, 5, 6], [1, 3, 4]]
> **Explanation:** This is one valid partition because both lists have size 3 and together contain every value from the input exactly once.

**Example 2:**

> **Input:** nums = [1, 2, 3, 4], k = 4
> **Output:** [[1], [2], [3], [4]]

**Example 3:**

> **Input:** nums = [1, 1, 2, 2], k = 2
> **Output:** [[2, 1], [1, 2]]

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of shuffling the array first to ensure randomness, then slicing it into equal-sized groups.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a random shuffle algorithm like Fisher-Yates to permute the array before partitioning.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The main challenge is ensuring each group has exactly n/k elements, handle the case where n is not divisible by k.

</details>
